scenario.summary: Threat actors exploit various vulnerabilities in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite to gain unauthenticated access, drop web shells, and manipulate mailbox and calendar data. This enables 'manufactured enterprise reality' where attackers impersonate executives, plant fraudulent documents, and use calendar invites to launch phishing or business email compromise attacks.

hunt.name: Zimbra BEC: Manufactured Reality and Manipulation
hunt.description: This hunt targets the manufactured reality phase of Business Email Compromise (BEC) within Zimbra environments. Unlike simple data theft, this attack involves altering the organization's system of record to gaslight users and facilitate fraud. We hunt for two primary behavioral indicators: the use of Zimbra administrative tools to silently configure mail forwarding and server-initiated network connections to meeting platforms like Zoom. These patterns indicate an attacker is actively shaping the communication environment to prop up fraudulent narratives.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, vendor_name FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%zimbra%' OR LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%zimbra%')
config.description: Identify the hosts running Zimbra to narrow the behavioral hunt to the mail backbone.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames acting as the Zimbra server. Silence indicates Zimbra is not managed or not present in software inventory.

primitive_config.label: Identify Zimbra collaboration servers
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, vendor_name FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%zimbra%' OR LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%zimbra%')
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames acting as the Zimbra server. Silence indicates Zimbra is not managed or not present in software inventory.

config.content: SELECT process_cmd_line, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, COUNT(*) AS runs, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%zmprov%' AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%modifyaccount%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%zimbraMailForwardingAddress%')) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY process_cmd_line HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC, runs DESC
config.description: Stack-count administrative commands that set mail forwarding to identify rare or unauthorized redirection across the Zimbra fleet.
config.expected_signal: Command lines redirected mail for specific users. A low host count suggests an attacker targeting specific mailboxes rather than global policy changes.

primitive_config.label: Prevalence of mail forwarding commands

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, dst_endpoint_hostname, process_name, COUNT(*) AS connections, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (instr(',' || '{{meeting_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(dst_endpoint_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, dst_endpoint_hostname, process_name ORDER BY connections DESC
config.description: Identify Zimbra servers initiating connections to external meeting platforms, indicating potential calendar invitation manipulation.
config.expected_signal: Connections from the Zimbra backend to Zoom, Teams, or Google Meet. Servers typically do not connect to these directly; users do from endpoints.
